arxiv-1906-10732.title: The Difficulty of Training Sparse Neural Networks
arxiv-1906-10732.creator: Utku Evci, Fabian Pedregosa, Aidan N. Gomez, Erich Elsen
arxiv-1906-10732.description: Abstract We investigate the difficulties of training sparse neural networks and make new observations about optimization dynamics and the energy landscape within the sparse regime. Recent work of Gale et al. 2019 ; Liu et al. 2018 has shown that sparse ResNet-50 architectures trained on ImageNet-2012 dataset converge to solutions that are significantly worse than those found by pruning.

arxiv-2107-05701.title: Scale-dependent irreversibility in living matter
arxiv-2107-05701.creator: Tzer Han Tan, Garrett A. Watson, Yu-Chen Chao, Junang Li, Todd R. Gingrich, Jordan M. Horowitz, Nikta Fakhri
arxiv-2107-05701.description: Abstract Abstract A defining feature of living matter is the ability to harness energy to self-organize multiscale structures whose functions are facilitated by irreversible nonequilibrium dynamics [ 1 ] . While progress has been made in elucidating the underlying principles, what remains unclear is the role that thermodynamics plays in shaping these structures and their ensuing functions.

arxiv-2306-08510.title: Permutation Invariant Recurrent Neural Networks for Sound Source Tracking Applications
arxiv-2306-08510.description: Abstract Many multi-source localization and tracking models based on neural networks use one or several recurrent layers at their final stages to track the movement of the sources. Conventional recurrent neural networks (RNNs), such as the long short-term memories (LSTMs) or the gated recurrent units (GRUs), take a vector as their input and use another vector to store their state.

arxiv-2403-04431.title: Boosting Fairness and Robustness in Over-the-Air Federated Learning* Thanks: * This work has been funded by the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG, German Research Foundation) under Germany’s Excellence Strategy – EXC 2002/1 “Science of Intelligence” – project number 390523135. Thanks: 1 H.Y. Oksu
arxiv-2403-04431.creator: Halil Yigit Oksuz, Fabio Molinari, Henning Sprekeler, Jörg Raisch
arxiv-2403-04431.description: Abstract Over-the-Air Computation is a beyond-5G communication strategy that has recently been shown to be useful for the decentralized training of machine learning models due to its efficiency. In this paper, we propose an Over-the-Air federated learning algorithm that aims to provide fairness and robustness through minmax optimization.

arxiv-2410-12292.title: How much do contextualized representations encode long-range context?
arxiv-2410-12292.creator: Simeng Sun, Cheng-Ping Hsieh
arxiv-2410-12292.description: Abstract We analyze contextual representations in neural autoregressive language models, emphasizing long-range contexts that span several thousand tokens. Our methodology employs a perturbation setup and the metric Anisotropy-Calibrated Cosine Similarity , to capture the degree of contextualization of long-range patterns from the perspective of representation geometry.

arxiv-2412-17613.title: Can Stability be Detrimental? Better Generalization through Gradient Descent Instabilities
arxiv-2412-17613.creator: Lawrence Wang, Stephen J. Roberts
arxiv-2412-17613.description: Abstract Traditional analyses of gradient descent optimization show that, when the largest eigenvalue of the loss Hessian - often referred to as the sharpness - is below a critical learning-rate threshold, then training is ‘stable’ and training loss decreases monotonically.

arxiv-2501-02760.title: CHAT: Beyond Contrastive Graph Transformer for Link Prediction in Heterogeneous Networks
arxiv-2501-02760.creator: Shengming Zhang, Le Zhang, Jingbo Zhou, Hui Xiong
arxiv-2501-02760.description: Abstract . Link prediction in heterogeneous networks is crucial for understanding the intricacies of network structures and forecasting their future developments. Traditional methodologies often face significant obstacles, including over-smoothing—wherein the excessive aggregation of node features leads to the loss of critical structural details—and a dependency on human-defined meta-paths, which necessitate extensive domain knowledge and can be inherently restrictive.

arxiv-2512-05974.title: The rationality of radical pair mechanism in real biological systems
arxiv-2512-05974.creator: Xiaoyu Chen, Haibin Liu, Jianming Cai
arxiv-2512-05974.description: Abstract The radical pair mechanism (RPM) in the chemical magnetic compass model is considered to be one of the most promising candidates for the avian magnetic navigation, and quantum needle phenomenon further boosts the navigation precision to a new high level.

arxiv-2602-06801.title: On the Non-Identifiability of Steering Vectors in Large Language Models
arxiv-2602-06801.creator: Sohan Venkatesh Ashish Mahendran Kurapath
arxiv-2602-06801.description: Abstract Activation steering methods are widely used to control large language model (LLM) behavior and are often interpreted as revealing meaningful internal representations. This interpretation assumes steering directions are identifiable and uniquely recoverable from input–output behavior. We show that, under white-box single-layer access, steering vectors are fundamentally non-identifiable due to large equivalence classes of behaviorally indistinguishable interventions.

pmc-10587535.title: The effect of increasing temperature on simulated nanocomposites reinforced with SWBNNs and its effect on characteristics related to mechanics and the physical attributes using the MDs approach
pmc-10587535.creator: Somayeh Tavasolikejani, Ashkan Farazin
pmc-10587535.description: This study examines the effect of increasing temperature (300, 350, 400, 450 and 500 K) on simulated nanocomposites reinforced with exploration of the impact of single-walled boron nitride nanotubes (SWBNNTs) on both the mechanical properties (including Young's modulus, Poisson's ratio, shear modulus, and bulk modulus) and the physical property of density, achieved through molecular dynamics (MDs) simulations.

pmc-11347411.title: Polydatin attenuated neuropathic pain and motor dysfunction following spinal cord injury in rats by employing its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects
pmc-11347411.creator: Faezeh Sadat Bagheri Bavandpouri, Atefeh Azizi, Fatemeh Abbaszadeh, Amir Kiani, Mohammad Hosein Farzaei, Ehsan Mohammadi-Noori, Sajad Fakhri, Javier Echeverría
pmc-11347411.description: BackgroundConsidering the complex pathological mechanisms behind spinal cord injury (SCI) and the adverse effects of present non-approved drugs against SCI, new studies are needed to introduce novel multi-target active ingredients with higher efficacy and lower side effects. Polydatin (PLD) is a naturally occurring stilbenoid glucoside recognized for its antioxidative and anti-inflammatory properties.

pmc-11401135.description: This study aims to detect Escherichia coli which encodes beta-lactamase Cefotaxime (blaCTX-M) gene from the reproductive tract of Bali cattle with repeat breeder cases. This research was conducted from June to August 2021 using 16 Bali cattle with repeat breeder cases.

pmc-11524973.title: Identification of immune microenvironment subtypes and clinical risk biomarkers for osteoarthritis based on a machine learning model
pmc-11524973.creator: Bao Li, Yang Shen, Songbo Liu, Hong Yuan, Ming Liu, Haokun Li, Tonghe Zhang, Shuyuan Du, Xinwei Liu
pmc-11524973.description: BackgroundOsteoarthritis (OA) is a degenerative disease with a high incidence worldwide. Most affected patients do not exhibit obvious discomfort symptoms or imaging findings until OA progresses, leading to irreversible destruction of articular cartilage and bone. Therefore, developing new diagnostic biomarkers that can reflect articular cartilage injury is crucial for the early diagnosis of OA.

pmc-12775628.title: Is L5/S1 interbody fusion necessary with concurrent iliac fixation for long segment spinal fusion constructs?—a systematic review of biomechanical studies
pmc-12775628.creator: Alexander J. Schupper, Michael Tawil, Han Jo Kim, Andrew C. Hecht, Jeremy M. Steinberger, James D. Lin
pmc-12775628.description: BackgroundLong segment fusion for adult spinal deformity (ASD) has a significant rate pseudoarthrosis, which may be in part due to the mechanical forces across the lumbosacral junction (LSJ). Placement of an interbody cage at the L5–S1 disc space and iliac fixation are two strategies to decrease strain at the L5–S1 level.

The corporation and its State, regional, and local subdivisions have the exclusive right to use the name “AMVETS (American Veterans)” and seals, emblems, and badges the corporation adopts.
